A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedAux research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on six graph datasets, synthetic client-similarity experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds membership-inference attacks and experiments integrating APV into other federated-learning methods.

M1.justification: The core FedAux algorithm, loss, and aggregation procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds limited adaptations: replacing FED-PUB's functional similarity with APV and jointly training APV with the methods called GraphGTA and FedSage+.

E1.justification: The six graph datasets and synthetic client-similarity scenario are retained. v2 adds a membership-inference task on Cora, Pubmed, and ogbn-arxiv, extending evaluation to privacy attacks without introducing new graph datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine comparators. The new privacy comparison reuses FedGNN and FedGTA. Figure 4 tests APV adaptations of existing baselines rather than adding competitors against FedAux; its GraphGTA original scores match FedGTA in Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds an honest-but-curious server attack protocol using parameter/APV histories, member/non-member probes, and Attack AUC. It also specifies paired transferability comparisons under a common 10-client split. Existing classification splits, training budgets, and model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds two substantive analyses absent from v1: empirical membership-leakage testing and APV transferability across three baseline architectures. These expand scrutiny of privacy and applicability beyond FedAux itself. The original ablations and hyperparameter analyses in Appendix E are retained.

E5.justification: The new membership-inference results are explicitly averaged over five random seeds. Table 1 continues reporting means and standard deviations over three runs; this is not an increase in the original experiments' run count. No confidence intervals or significance tests accompany the new attack results.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports FedAux attack AUCs of 0.51, 0.52, and 0.49 on Cora, Pubmed, and ogbn-arxiv; Figure 4 adds paired original/APV accuracy results. In Table 1, Pubmed with 10 clients changes from 85.43±0.20 to 86.43±0.20, reversing its ranking against FED-PUB's unchanged 86.09±0.17. The appendix ablation retains 85.43±0.29. Other matched main-table results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.3, their assumptions and proofs, and the non-IIDness definitions remain substantively unchanged. The existing complexity analysis moves from Appendix B into the main text. Notation and cross-reference wording changes do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims about APV-based personalization, parameter-only communication, theoretical guarantees, and predictive performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the attack results as evidence against membership leakage and the transferability results as supporting generic APV integration. New Appendix F explicitly identifies quadratic local kernel computation as a scalability limitation and proposes low-rank or Nyström approximations as future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the abstract and specifies the attack classifier as a two-layer MLP with hidden size 64, trained by maximum likelihood. The existing backbone, hyperparameters, communication schedules, and hardware disclosures in Appendix D.2 are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds comparisons with FedSSP, FedEgo, PFGNAS, and FedGrAINS, emphasizing privacy and computational tradeoffs. Membership-inference references and Commute Graph Neural Networks are added, while the Proximity Enhanced Graph Neural Networks citation is removed. The established positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Changes include expanded explanations, relocation of complexity analysis, new limitations and acknowledgements sections, numeric citation style, revised concatenated-embedding notation, and updated authorship and conference-header text.

P2.justification: v2 adds the attack-results table and a three-panel transferability figure, expands Figure 1's caption, and adjusts table sizing and row order. Existing figures and appendix tables are retained with renumbering and relocation; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new privacy and transferability experiments provide useful evidence absent from v1, while code-access information and the explicit scalability limitation improve transparency. These gains are limited: the narrow attack evaluation does not establish general absence of leakage, and the revised Pubmed result in Table 1 conflicts with the retained value in Appendix Table 6.
